full_judgment:
22. The fundamental and basic presumption in the administration of criminal law and justice delivery system is that the accused should be presumed to be innocent till the charges are proved beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of clear, cogent, credible unimpeachable evidence. In a criminal trial, the burden of proving guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt always rests on the prosecution and on its failure, it cannot fall back upon the accused. In a criminal case, it is for, the on prosecution to bring the guilt home to the accused. 

 23. In the instant case the prosecution has taken alibi that the victim Jesmin loved Pashan Ali and she went to him and married him having registered kabinnama. When the accused has taken the plea of alibi, in such case the burden of proof lies on the appellant who substantially asserts that the victim Jesmin loved him and she went with him voluntarily. It is also decided in case of Soma Bhai vs State of Gujarat reported in 1975 SC 1453 that the plea of alibi has got to be proved by the defence to the satisfaction of the Court. It is stated in the case of State of Maharashtra vs Narsingarao Gangaram Pimple reported 1 CrLJ 1984 that the plea of alibi must be proved with absolute certainty. 

 24. Now let us see how far the respective parties have succeeded in proving their respective burden.
